# 94 of 100 apps can be agent toolkits today. The work is in review queues, not code.

> An agent researched auth, access, API surface and MCP for 100 apps, citing a page for every answer. Only 4 need a business conversation and 2 have no usable API. The usual blocker is app review (30 apps): a developer can build freely, but shipping to other people's accounts needs the vendor's sign-off.

## Data
- [apps.json](data/apps.json): all 100 verified records with evidence URLs and quotes
- [apps.csv](data/apps.csv): the same as a flat table

## Patterns
- **OAuth2 dominates, and most OAuth apps also take a key** 78 apps offer OAuth2, and it is the primary method for 63. Only 8 offer OAuth2 alone: 62 also accept an API key or personal token, which is the fast path for a prototype. 19 apps have no OAuth at all, mostly data, scraping and AI-native tools, where one shared key per customer is the model.
- **The common blocker is publishing, not access** 31 apps let a developer build and test for free but put a review between the app and other people's accounts: Meta, Google Ads, LinkedIn, Intuit, Shopify, Zendesk, HubSpot. 18 more need a paid plan or run only on a trial. Hard gates are rare: 9 are partner-only, sales-only or have no API.
- **Where self-serve lives, and where it doesn't** Self-serve access (free or trial) is most common in Developer, Infra and Data platforms (9/10), Productivity and Project Management (9/10). The fewest self-serve apps are in Support and Helpdesk (2/10), Finance and Fintech (2/10), where ad platforms, marketplaces and fintech guard production access behind review or contracts.
- **Vendors are shipping their own MCP servers** 86 of the 100 publish an official MCP server, 79 of them hosted at a URL with OAuth. Another 12 have only community servers. This was also the field the first pass got wrong most often: several servers launched in 2026 and are announced on pages search hasn't caught up with.
- **Easy wins versus outreach** 2 apps are ready now with self-serve credentials. 10 need a partnership, a sales conversation or a different approach because there is no API. That second list is a business-development queue, not an engineering one.

## Accuracy
- Hand-audited sample: 20 apps x 8 fields. Research agent alone: 77.5%. After verification loops: 87.5%.
